fields.v: SkillReducer (proposed; no version). Compared: original skill (A), no skill (D), LLMLingua, direct LLM compression, truncation, random sentence removal; ablation variants C1-C4

Agent skills (Anthropic skill protocol: SKILL.md with routing description and Markdown body, optional reference files, scripts out of scope). Output: compressed routing description; compressed core body (always loaded); on-demand reference modules (examples.md, templates.md, background.md, deduplicated references) annotated with 'when' clause and 3-5 topic keywords

Stage 1 (routing layer): segment description into semantic clauses -> DDMIN with simulated routing oracle (TF-IDF distractors + LLM adversarial skill) -> paraphrase/polish -> real trigger validation via Claude Code CLI with selective restore or fallback; generate missing descriptions. Stage 2 (body): classify paragraphs (core rule, background, example, template, redundant) -> type-specific compression -> cross-file deduplication -> annotate references -> Gate 1 faithfulness check -> Gate 2 task evaluation with feedback loop (promote items to core, max 2 iterations)

fields.v: Paired design per skill: conditions D (no skill), A (original), C (compressed, references via read_file, max 6 tool calls). Baselines at equal token budget. Held constant: tasks, evaluator model (Qwen3.5, separate API key from compressor DeepSeek-V3), temperature 0 for classification. Acceptance tests: assertion-based scripts for code tasks, LLM-judge rubrics, SkillsBench pytest verifiers. Repetitions: one run per task (not stated otherwise); bootstrap CIs. Human intervention: none

C > A on average (0.742 vs 0.722, Wilcoxon p=0.002, d=0.107, small); holds without ceiling cases (p=0.010); text says gain larger for long official skills (+11.8 pp vs +1.1 pp community), but Table III gives Official 0.743 -> 0.831 (+8.8 pp). SkillReducer beats all four compression baselines (one-sided sign tests, p<=0.003). Taxonomy classification key (C4 retention 0.919, -6.8 pp). Transfers to 5 models (mean retention 0.965) and OpenCode (0.944). Of 84 regressions, ~33% true compression failures (4.7% of skills). End-to-end input savings 26.8% (best case)

rev.why: The +11.8 pp official-skill gain in the text does not match Table III (A 0.743, C 0.831 = +8.8 pp); the community figure (+1.1 pp) does match

fields.v: Distinguished SkillReducer from baselines and ablations; SkillsBench did not distinguish (ceiling: D 86/87). Repeatable: single runs, bootstrap CIs and paired tests. Limitations stated: Gate 2 is both optimization signal and evaluation criterion (optimization-to-criterion); LLM randomness; only Anthropic skill protocol; five models from four families; Wild study without Gate 2

Generalization to other platforms (Cursor, Windsurf) and model families (Llama) untested; Wild sample lacks task evaluation; example-as-specification failure mode (implicit rules in examples); skill obsolescence (10.7%) motivates adaptive skill lifecycle management

Inconsistencies: feedback loop recovery reported as 31/38 = 81.6% (p. 9) but 27/38 = 71.1% in Appendix E (p. 13); official-skill gain +11.8 pp in text vs +8.8 pp from Table III (0.743 -> 0.831); end-to-end savings given as 26.8% (best case), 43.2% and 57.4% (theoretical) in different places, and Appendix E calls 26.8%-43.2% 'our empirical measurement' although 43.2% is derived; cross-compressor retention for DeepSeek-V3 is 0.896 while Table VIII (same compressor, 30 skills) gives 0.965 mean and no evaluator below 0.939, with the fixed evaluator not named; SkillsBench body reduction given as 75.0% mean per task in the text, -74.1% in Figure 4, while 359K -> 84K is 76.6% in aggregate (may be different aggregations). Figure 4 label reads 'SkillsBench (17 tasks)' vs 84/87 in text (pdftotext; check figure). Tables III, IV, VI, VIII rebuilt from pdftotext column order; Table VII (sensitivity) jumbled, values not used. Agent harness for main evaluation is the authors' own pipeline with Qwen3.5; Claude Code CLI only for routing validation. Tool to be released upon acceptance (no link). No pre-registration. Languages: skills in Markdown; code tasks in Python
